claims.text: Advanced metadynamics or replica-exchange methods can reduce the computational cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties in multicomponent high-entropy systems.
These enhanced-sampling methods can maintain fidelity in free-energy evaluations while reducing computational cost.
Advanced metadynamics or replica exchange will sample phase space more efficiently.
More efficient phase-space sampling enables better exploration of the free-energy landscape.
Better exploration of the free-energy landscape will provide accurate free-energy evaluations without the extensive computational cost of traditional molecular dynamics.
The proposed methods will reduce computational cost by approximately 50–70% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed methods will retain fidelity similar to TOR-TILD results for elemental and binary systems.
Current free-energy methodologies rely on explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Traditional methods are currently limited for multicomponent high-entropy systems at high temperatures.
The hypothesis applies to multicomponent high-entropy systems under high-temperature conditions.
Effectiveness may vary with system complexity.
A cost reduction below 50%, or significantly lower free-energy fidelity than traditional molecular dynamics, would falsify the hypothesis.
